text:
marco: quick follow-up from yesterday's cp handoff spike. alternative idea: use a lightweight 'soft-marker' for endpoint handoffs instead of immediate deletes. goal: reduce route flip churn during cross-region handovers.

anika: short question: soft-marker vs tombstone? semantics different?

marco: semantics: soft-marker = annotate endpoint as 'possibly-moving' + include holder-lease meta (region, epoch, lease_expiry). routing decisions can prefer fallback but continue to use local for a short probation. tombstone felt too final.

devon: interesting. how do we encode keyspace? separate key or flag on endpoint value?

marco: prefer flag on the same key: keeps single read path: key = endpoint/<tenant>/<id>, value includes "addr,ports,meta,soft_marker":{"owner":"cp-eu","epoch":42,"since":1680000000}. avoids extra scans.

priya: sounds simpler for clients. but watch fanout will now send larger blobs. any perf hit?

marco: we measured ~6% increase in watch payload size in our local tests for a blob with soft_marker; watch throughput still fine. downside: clients must parse marker field. we will make marker optional and compact.

kevin: routing logic: what should relay do on seeing marker? immediate fallback or attempt local with degraded score?

marco: relay scoring: if marker.since + probation_ttl > now => treat local with penalty + start async probe to confirm reachability. if probe fails OR marker expired => fallback to global-relay. default probation_ttl 3m.

anika: probes are expensive at scale. what do probes look like? single TCP handshake? quick health ping?

marco: cheap probe: single SYN+ACK timeout ~250ms, no payload. probe jittered and rate-limited per-tenant. only run when relay sees a marker for the first time or after marker changes owner.

priya: state reconciliation: what about CP split-brain where two CPs both set marker with different epochs?

kevin: use existing cp-lease-holder contract. any marker write must include lease_id and epoch. marker-clear only allowed by holder or after CAS with lease check. conflict resolution: higher epoch wins, older marker extended until resolved.

devon: sample watch event for clients?

marco: watch line (single-line JSON) we plan to emit: {"type":"PUT","key":"endpoint/tenant123/e1","val":"...","marker":{"owner":"cp-eu","epoch":42,"since":1680000000,"probation_ttl":180}}. clients should treat type=PUT with marker present as special.

anika: older clients won't understand marker. compatibility strategy?

marco: watchers get best-effort: older clients treat it as normal update and keep cache. we'll roll client bump that reads marker and applies degraded behaviour. server will also honor a header `x-endpoint-marker-supported` from relays to gate advanced behaviour.

priya: GC/sweep behaviour? we need to cleanup stale markers on failed handoffs.

marco: two mechanisms: (1) lease-driven expiry: marker has lease_expiry and is auto-invalidated when lease lapses; (2) background reconciler runs every 60s and removes orphan markers where lease not present or epoch mismatch. Reconciler uses CAS against endpoint key. Emits metrics softmarker.gc.*.

kevin: operator controls: per-tenant toggle and global feature flag. add flag `features.soft_marker=true` in controlplane config. Also tenant-level `soft_marker.mode=probation|immediate` for testing.

devon: observability & SLO safety: alert windows?

marco: proposed metrics/alerts: softmarker.count > 1000 sustained over 10m => alert. softmarker.reconcile_failures > 10/min => alert. watch.latency.p50/p95 increase after rollout should be tracked.

anika: rollback plan?

marco: rollout steps: feature-flagged deploy to cp-local in us-west, enable per-tenant toggle for a canary tenant, monitor metrics for 1h, expand to region, then global. rollback: flip feature-flag off + trigger force-clean reconciler to strip markers if needed.

ops-bot: runbook reminder: runbook link https://runbooks.internal/soft-marker-handbook (review required).

priya: tests to add: dual-writer race sim, watch-fanout-canary, probe-thundering simulation, reconcile-throughput test. please record perf numbers in the PR.

kevin: small nit: naming. 'soft-marker' in infra, call 'soft-handoff' in docs? consistency matters.

marco: agreed. use 'soft-marker' in telemetry and code, and 'soft-handoff' in external docs.

devon: one more: client cache TTL interaction. clients may keep stale entries for TTL. should we shorten default client cache TTL when marker present?

marco: yes: convention: when marker present, clients should honour a dynamic cache TTL = min(configured_ttl, probation_ttl). we'll publish this in client SDK docs and add header `x-cache-ttl-suggested`.

anika: sounds good. can you open PR with clear tests + config YAML?

marco: will do. sample config snippet for rollout (YAML):

```yaml
controlplane:
  features:
    soft_marker: true
  soft_marker:
    default_probation_ttl_sec: 180
    reconcile_interval_sec: 60
    per_tenant_rate_limit: 50
```

marco: tagging @infra-team for runbook and @sdk for client SDK changes. will post PR link when ready.

ops-bot: deploy note: deploy/cp-soft-marker-feature 2026-04-02T12:00Z by marco :rocket:

marco: thanks all. feedback welcome, leaning to start canary next week.
